findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate the audit log datetime field
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any nonempty optimized response raises TypeError when build_cursor computes its keys. value_from_cursor also returns a number unchanged rather than converting it to a datetime for the SQL comparison. Use the DateTimePaginator key encoding and decoding for this endpoint; otherwise enabling optimized_pagination breaks audit log retrieval.

findings.title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The advanced-feature branch passes a negative cursor offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'); it does not handle these boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature always fails for the audit log queryset. Validate and reject unsupported offsets as a pagination error, or implement reverse traversal using supported queries rather than negative slicing.
